title: Your traffic sources have a half-life: favor long half-life channels over spikes
summary: Rob Walling argues that every traffic source decays, and sorts them by half-life: advertising (zero), social/viral spikes like Hacker News and Twitter (short, about 12 hours), and SEO, email and RSS (long, years). Bootstrappers should not rely on ads or viral spikes, and should convert short half-life traffic into long half-life assets like an email list.

principles.text: All traffic sources decay; classify them by half-life: zero (ads), short (social, viral), long (SEO, email, RSS).
principles.quote: The concept centers around the idea that traffic sources decay over time. Some decay faster than others, but they all die out eventually if you don’t invest time to maintain them.

principles.text: Consistent organic traffic can out-deliver viral spikes over time, despite far smaller daily peaks.
principles.quote: the compounding nature of the consistent organic traffic actually brought in around 70% of each of the other two peaks.

principles.text: If you're bootstrapping, don't plan to advertise: ads build no traffic equity.
principles.quote: Advertising doesn’t build traffic “equity.” It doesn’t sustain at all. Once you stop paying you stop receiving clicks.

principles.text: Use viral, short half-life sources for launches and announcements, but don't build the business on them.
principles.quote: But if your business relies on these sources to sustain itself you had better be an insanely talented buzz builder

principles.text: Long half-life sources (SEO, email, RSS) are the holy grail for a business that doesn't need constant customer acquisition spend.
principles.quote: If you want to build a business that does not require a heavy, ongoing, constant investment in finding new customers…focus on long half-life traffic sources

principles.text: Convert fleeting viral traffic into a long half-life asset, such as an email list.
principles.quote: Facebook and Groupon, two of the most talked-about companies of the past year, are actually highly-optimized email marketing firms masquerading as viral marketing firms
